title: Warranty Coverage General Conditions: Start Date, Term Counting, Registration and Rental Cap
content:
Four general conditions of Warranty Coverage are the same in all six Ridgeline plans. They fix the date terms run from, how a term in years is counted, how a registration comes about and the cap on every term while the home is a rental.

| Plan | Date every term counts from | How a term in years is counted | Rental-property cap on every term | Registered automatically at installation |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Ridgeline Limited Warranty | installation completion date | through the day before the ending anniversary | 10 years | yes |
| Ridgeline Limited Plus Warranty | installation completion date | through the day before the ending anniversary | 10 years | yes |
| Ridgeline Lifetime Limited Warranty | installation completion date | through the day before the ending anniversary | 10 years | yes |
| Ridgeline Lifetime Plus Warranty | installation completion date | through the day before the ending anniversary | 10 years | yes |
| Ridgeline Lifetime Premier Warranty | installation completion date | through the day before the ending anniversary | 10 years | yes |
| Ridgeline Owner-to-Owner Lifetime Warranty | installation completion date | through the day before the ending anniversary | 10 years | yes |

## The conditions in words

1. **Coverage start date.** Every term is counted from the date the installation was completed.
2. **Counting a term in years.** Coverage runs through the day before the anniversary that ends the term.
3. **Rental cap.** While the home is used as a rental property, every term, a lifetime term included, is capped at 10 years counted from the coverage start date.
4. **Registration.** Coverage is registered automatically when the installation is completed; the customer files nothing to register it.

## Illustrations (hypothetical dates)

- An installation completed on 12 September in a given year starts every term on that 12 September.
- A 5-year term starting on 12 September runs through 11 September five years later, the day before the fifth anniversary.
- In a home used as a rental property, a lifetime frame term and a 20-year insulated glass term are both capped at 10 years from the coverage start date; a 2-year screen term stays 2 years, since a cap never lengthens a shorter term.
